question: I am trying to get a Powerflex 40P running. I removed the enable and am using terminal 1 as an enable input. We are using devicenet to send it commands. I see that is working since bit 10 is on. Everything is enabled and the drive is ready. I issue the start command and get nothing from the drive. The run light does not come on and it still reads 000 on the display. Any advice???
solution: Yes - set P38 to '5' for the comm port. Make sure not to turn on the start bit until the ready bit is on. Only then make the transition from off to on. Edit - I now see that comms (5) is the default setting for P38, interesting. [earlier in thread, same author]: Can you specify what you have tied to the control terminals. It sounds like you just have the terminal 1 input tied (either high or low) to the appropriate enable voltage (possibly through a contact? - which is fine). In the setup you must specify that the control is coming from the communication, not from the front panel or from a terminal (P036). You may also be controlling the frequency from the communication which you must specify also (P038).Make sure the drive is stoped when making these parameter changes. [after SandyB reported partial progress, 'That helped so that now the run light comes on but the frequency on the display stays 000?']: I don't have the MODBUS documentation for the PF40P. We always write the frequency directly. Set the speed control back to '4' and reset. Then try the speed pre-selection in the control word.
confirmation: All set and thanks for the help
notes: Product line is PowerFlex 40P (a variant of PowerFlex 40 / Rockwell 22D family), not plain PowerFlex 40 — listing as PowerFlex 40 per the allowed product list. Multi-step exchange: b_carlton gave parameter guidance twice (P036 then P038), SandyB reported partial fix, b_carlton gave the final speed-control-word fix, then SandyB's final post 'All set and thanks for the help' is the confirmation. question: Hello everyone, I'm working on a project with an Allen-Bradley Micro820 PLC and PV800 HMI. This is my first time using A-B controllers, and I'm having trouble connecting and downloading my ladder diagram. Thus far, my full program is 13 rungs, and builds successfully. I've also written a test program that's just one input triggering one output, which also builds successfully. However, I haven't been able to download either program. When I plug into my PLC with a Cat5 patch cable, my PC can see the PLC in both RSLinx Classic (using Ethernet/IP Driver) and in Connected Components Workbench. It successfully detects the PLC IP address, which changes each time I power cycle the PLC, matching the default DHCP IP setting for these PLCs. However, nothing happens when I press the "Connect" button.
solution: When you goto setup connection path and browse, you should get a selection of network(drivers you want to browse) this should be one of them "AB_ETHIP_1", if that is not listed this is your problem, if it is listed click on it. This should then should the IP address of your PLC if it does make sure it is highlighted then click OK, this will then connect to the PLC. Now this will only work if your Laptop(PC) is on the same subnet as the PLC. ... Here's how to set PLC to static if you can't connect. On a sd card create a "Configmefirst.txt" file and in that file this should be. [PM] [IPA=192.168.2.101] [SNM=255.255.255.0] [GWA=192.168.2.1] [END] Save and insert into PLC and do a power cycle, Plc will set it's ip to the information in the file.
confirmation: So I entered the above text (with IP, subnet mask, and GWA to match my computer settings...), saved it to the microSD card, inserted in the PLC and power cycled. ... I selected the new driver and was able to connect and download my project. It looks like my program is running from my brief test, thank you for the help!
notes: ConfigMeFirst.txt is the Micro820 SD-card network bootstrap mechanism documented in the Micro820 user manual (2080-UM001A); AB_ETHIP_1 is the EtherNet/IP driver name browsed in RSLinx/CCW. Clean single-asker confirmation, no attribution ambiguity.

question: One of my customers has an overwrapping machine with a PowerFlex 40 controlling the infeed conveyor motor. They want to decrease the decel setting (parameter P40) from 0.5 to 0.3. They are able to change it from the keypad on the drive, and it works on the new setting. Once power is cycled though, it returns to the previous 0.5 value. The drive is on a Devicenet network, so I'm guessing the changed value is getting overwritten? If so, then by what? In the .dnt file, there is no lock symbol present at parameter 40. What does the little 'scales' icon mean?
solution: Very likely the PowerFlex 40 has been configured for 'Auto-Device Replacement', in which the scanner holds the parameters and checks each time it makes a connection to be sure the parameter checksum is the same. If it's not, the scanner sends the saved parameters down to the drive. ... On the ADR tab for the 1769-SDN, you'll see that Nodes 3, 4, 6, and 7 are configured for ADR Configuration Recovery. That explains why the scanner was putting the saved values back into the drive. You can just un-check the Configuration Recovery box to allow changes to be made to the drive, or make the change and re-load the Device Configuration and save the updated values to the 1769-SDN's ADR memory.
confirmation: Just to follow up, I FINALLY found time to visit this customer yesterday, and this solved it. Thanks!
notes: Eric Nelson's confirming post is explicitly tagged 'OP' in the rendered page, so attribution to the original asker is unambiguous. Parameter P40 (Decel Time) is the symptom; 'ADR Configuration Recovery' (a 1769-SDN DeviceNet scanner setting) is the actual fix identifier.

question: Gents I'm working on a small project here and the customer requested to control the drive with 4-20mA by using Micro820 Analog output 4-20mA, Module 2080-OF2. After getting all the logic up and running the only issue I have is I can't get 4-20mA to present on the output? even checked with Ammeter on the output of the module I can't see anything. Typically after doing scaling the output is REAL data type but the module only accepts UINT, and by using UNIT going to lose some data precision.
solution: The 2080-OF2 has 12-bit resolution, and the output range is 0 to 65535, so 4mA will be around 13107, and 20mA will be around 65535. ... If you write a UDINT value of 65535 to an -OF2 channel in the Micro820 program, the output current signal should be near 20mA. If you send a UDINT value of 0, the output current should be near 0mA. If you send a UDINT value of 13107 (=65535/5), the output current should be near 4mA (=20mA/5).
confirmation: Thank you guys for the Help. it finally worked with this setup 13107 = 4mA 65535 = 20mA I typically use an Ammeter to see the 4-20mA, but here little different method The output is a Varying voltage. after you connect it to the drive, it will "Covert" to Current because of the input resistance of the VFD. Appreciate all help
notes: Confirming post is explicitly marked 'Thread Starter' (Al-Naseri) in the rendered page. Count values 13107/65535 map directly to the 4-20mA scaling documented for the 2080-OF2 plug-in module.

question: Hello, I am trying to connect a 0-5v pressure sensor to the Micro 810, but I am not getting a clear input voltage reading. I connected the sensor signal wire to terminal I_04 and set the input to AI:00. I am wondering if I am not getting a reading because the Micro 810 wants either a 4-20ma or 0-10v signal. Any help would be appreciated.
solution: From what I have found the analog input is 12 bit, so it goes from 0V=0 to 10V=4095, so if your scaler input range is only from 0.5-4.5 that's probably the reason you don't see any change, try the 0 and 4095 as input values. Also make sure your pressure sensor shares the same DC common as the PLC
confirmation: This is probably obvious to most people on here, but I thought I'd explain what I did to fix this. First problem was I had the wrong input selected. The AI option wasn't listed at first. _IO_EM_DI_00 _IO_EM_AI_00 I also had the common (or negative 5v) wire in the wrong terminal. I switched it from terminal 3 to terminal 8. Boom! It worked. Thanks everyone.

question: Hi guys I am new to the threads and relatively new to the world of PLC programming. During a recent programming session, I was using the Micro820 in DHCP mode when I blindly tried to configure a static IP address. In doing so and while connected, I managed to remove all IP address settings from the controller and now I can not connect, the ENET light is not showing any signs of life when I plug in (it should show green even without config) and windows diagnostics is telling me that my device does not have IP config. ... Can somebody tell me if there is another way to connect directly through the comms port.
solution: If you have genuinely disabled the controller's Ethernet port ... then the best way to get it reset is to connect to the RS-232 port. It's a screw-terminal port but if you have an RS-232 port available (built in or USB adapter) you can simply cut the end off a cable, verify the pins 2,3,5 conductors, and wire it in.

question: I am trying to read and write specific parameters from a Powerflex 525 to a Micrologix 1100. I followed the instructions from a Knowledgebase and was able to do it. By using a CIP Generic - Generic Get Attribute Single MSG I can read parameter 7 for instance without any trouble. I tried to change the instance in the MSG to read another parameter (388 to be exact). It did not work. The MSG sent back an error: error code (in upper byte of MGx:y.22) was returned by Comms module or CIP device. I switched it back to 7 and it was fine.
solution: The correct data type is DINT. One Byte is INT Two Bytes is DINT Four Bytes is LINT [and, after LURBY reported that DINT/LINT guesses still failed:] The "L" data file [known as Long] is 32 bits. Try creating one of those to send your 4 bytes to. [Joe E. added:] I'd try the "L" data type as the destination if it will let you, like NevergoldMel suggested.
confirmation: I used a "L" data type yesterday and it did not work. I tried it again today but instead of putting the instance of 388 in the (hex) box like the other parameters I put it in the (dec) box. That did the trick. Thank you all for your help.
notes: Every LURBY post in the raw HTML is explicitly tagged 'Author', so attribution to the original asker is unambiguous. The actual fix combined the suggested 'L' (Long/32-bit) data type with LURBY's own discovery that the parameter instance had to go in the decimal box, not the hex box, in the MSG instruction dialog. question: Hi all, I am looking to find out where my problem is regarding this situation. To my knowledge I have all the correct settings, but when I remove the Modbus Connection from my VSD, the VSD does not show a Comms Fault, even though i set it to 'fault if comms loss' any ideas? My PowerFlex Settings are: Start Source =5 Comms Port Speed Ref = 5 Comms Port Comms Data Rate = 4 (19.2 K, and is matched with my program configuration) Node Address = 1 (Unique address) Comms Format = 0 RTU 8 N -1 I also checked Parameter D012 which correctly shows the value of 55 confirming that the Control Source is Via Modbus Comms. With my really basic program running, I have also interogated d015, but I get a value of : 0000 without any activity, so its very hard to diagnose at the moment. Ps: Wiring to VSD is done exactly as RS485 Protocol in Appendix C of the 4M manual.
solution: What is the setting for U305, the Comm Loss Time ? The default is 5 seconds but it can be as large as 60. I don't think the Comm Loss Timer starts running until the controller receives its first Command message, even if that message doesn't contain a Start command. Is your message logic running successfully ? There's a very complete example of programming this Messaging in RA Knowledgebase 33774.
confirmation: Thank you Ken for your assistance. I used the code to make sure that code-wise things were fine. The problem was actually a weird one. I had a Rockwell document (not sure how old - called: PowerFlex Class Modbus Errors) showing that wiring should be from pin 4 & 5 of my AIC (was using AIC) to pin 1 & 8 of my Modbus connector. But the Rockwell link that you sent me showed, from 4 & 5 to 4 & 5. Which made all the difference. thanks for your help.
